paragraphs: John's disciples come to him a little worried. Everyone is going to Jesus now, and they sound like they expect John to mind. He doesn't. John says, "A man can receive only what is given him from heaven," and he reminds them he never claimed to be the Christ (John 3:27-28). His whole job was to point to Jesus, so a crowd walking toward Jesus means the job is working.

John calls himself the friend of the bridegroom, who "stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom's voice." Then he says, "That joy is mine, and it is now complete" (John 3:29). Then comes the line: "He must increase; I must decrease" (John 3:30). That's a joy I can bake with, friend. I make cookies for a feast that's all about the Lamb, and my name is nowhere on the guest list's favorite things. THE WHOLE POINT is that He gets the glory, and I get to be happy about it!

John tells us why Jesus is worth that kind of devotion. He comes from above, He testifies to what He has seen and heard, and "The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands" (John 3:31-35). So the choice in the last verse is simple and serious: "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him" (John 3:36). Baker, take the joy John had. Point to Jesus, believe in Him, and be glad when He gets bigger in your life and you get smaller.
